findings.claim: The split pin counts code lines that contain the exact text `split(want,`. A second split with other spacing gets past it. For example, a later code line `n = split( want, ids, "\n")` or `split(want , ids, "\n")` that splits again without forcing text is not counted, so splitPinProblem still sees exactly one line, equal to splitStatementLine, and returns "". Its doc says the statement 'cannot be reordered, left to a comment or written twice and still pass', and the gap behind 5e745160b611-5 F4 (keys built from split elements that were not made text) can then come back unseen. Matching any code line that holds `split(` and `want`, allowing blanks, would close it. -5 F4 is otherwise resolved as L82 says.

The new header text and PROVENANCE.md line 15 give ARG_MAX as '(getconf ARG_MAX, which follows the stack limit)'. As I recall the Linux kernel (fs/exec.c), it clamps the exec limit to at least 128 KiB and at most 3/4 of _STK_LIM (6 MiB). As I recall glibc, sysconf(_SC_ARG_MAX) returns the stack rlimit / 4 with no upper clamp. If so, on a host whose stack limit is above 24 MiB or unlimited, getconf ARG_MAX states a limit larger than the one exec applies. Below a 512 KiB stack it no longer follows the stack limit at all. A caller of this deployed contract (T4w) that sizes a call from getconf ARG_MAX could then pass the real limit and get the exec failure the text describes. This is not run and the kernel and glibc behavior was not re-read in this review. It rests on knowledge of those sources, so it is a SUGGESTION to word the parenthetical as an approximation or drop it.
